chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yusuf ibn Ya'qub al-Ja'fi narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Mihran narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

When the Abbasid ascends the rungs of Marwan's minbar, the dominion of the Abbasids will gradually decline. And he said: My father (meaning al-Baqir) said to me: 'There must be a fire from Azerbaijan that nothing will withstand. When that occurs, be the rear guards of your homes, and stay put as we stayed. When our man moves, hasten to him even if crawling. By Allah, as if I see him between the Corner and the Maqam, the people are swearing allegiance to him upon a new book, severe upon the Arabs.' He said: 'And woe to the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near.'

key_terms.أَحْلَاسَ بُيُوتِكُمْ: Rear guards of your homes (stay put)
key_terms.الرُّكْنُ وَالْمَقَامُ: The Corner and the Maqam (in Mecca)

ai.seo_question: What are the signs of the Abbasid decline and the rise of the Mahdi according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* links the political transition from the Umayyads to the Abbasids with the imminent rise of the Mahdi, emphasizing the 'Fire of Azerbaijan' as a precursor to his emergence. The Imam describes the Qa'im’s initial allegiance between the Rukn and Maqam in Mecca, noting his strict governance over the Arabs, which fulfills the prophetic warning of 'woe to the Arabs' from a specific evil. This highlights the Shia scholarly view of the Mahdi’s appearance as both a divine correction and a period of intense political upheaval.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (24) Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Sa’eed narrated from Ahmad bin Yousuf bin Ya’qoob al-Ju’fi from Issma’eel bin Mihran from al-Hasan bin Ali bin Abu Hamza from his father from Abu Baseer that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said:

“If the Abbasid ruler ascends the minbar of Marwan, the state of the Abbasids will begin to decline gradually. My father has said to me: “There must be a fire coming from Azerbaijan that will destroy everything. When that occurs, you are to stay at homes as long as we have stayed. When our man (al-Qa’im) rises, then hurry up to him even crawling. By Allah, as if I see him between the corner and the temple being paid homage to rule over the people with a new method. He will be severe with the Arabs. Woe unto the Arabs from a soon evil!”
